newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa rebounds slightly after sharp fall.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa rebounds slightly after sharp fall.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures rebounded slightly to end Friday morning trade with small gains as the market regained its composure after Thursday's fund-led sell-off, traders said.
In the much-awaited downward correction to the recent rally, prices dived to the lowest in two months on Thursday as funds liquidated big long positions.
Traders said there was some spill-over fund liquidation on Friday morning but the pace seemed to be slowing. The support in the market came from trade and manufacturer buying.
As expected, the second quarter Dutch and UK grind data, released earlier on Friday, showed a mixed trend and had no impact.
The Dutch data showed a 10.4 percent increase in grind year-on-year to 100,132 tonnes but the UK figures showed a 4.1 percent fall to 42,702 tonnes in the same period.
he German grind data are due to be released next week.
Benchmark September, which plunged to an intraday low of 1,000 stg on Thursday, recovered some ground to end Friday midday unchanged at 1,019 stg a tonne. It had ranged from between 1,018 and 1,037.
Traders said the contract looked safe above the 1,000 level before another round of selling knocks the prices lower.
Technically, September faces support at the chart gap of between 1,004 and 989 stg. On the upside, the major barrier is pegged at 1,100, which until Thursday was a key support.
But it could struggle to revisit this week's high of 1,170 stg, the peak of a rally that started in June when prices were lingering at 1,100 mark.

"The retracement is expected as the market is too overdone in the short-term," said a trader at a grinding firm. "It was purely a spec involvement. Most people in the industry didn't follow the rally."
Volume reached 4,570 lots, again dominted by September contract. July/September widened to 15 stg from five stg on Thursday while Sept/Dec held at around 22-23 stg.
The New York market is closed on Friday for the Fourth of July holiday, reopening on Monday. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
